information.description:
The biggest of the baddest, and damn near unkillable. Max-Tac Heavys are called as such mostly for their hulking size and impenetrable armor as opposed to their armament, which is only slightly lighter than what their full-bore military counterparts use. Still, they pack a brutal punch, and can withstand a truly unfathomable amount of firepower before they fall.

From Corgo's 77 Collection: Mooks by Corgopolis (Max-Tac).

Throwing hands, does not ignore half armor.

Sometimes all you need is a warning shot to scare off your attacker, but if that doesn't work, you'll need something more convincing. The M2067 Defender from Constitutional Arms will almost certainly do the trick. This light machine gun was designed for all the righteous, upstanding citizens living in dangerous neighborhoods. With a remarkably high firing rate, large magazine and automatic reload, in the right conditions someone holding one of these could take out a whole army.

Cost: 1,000eb (Very Expensive)

Concealable: No

Requires BODY 8+ to wield unless Mounted, and BODY 10+ or paired Cyberarms to not reduce the user’s MOVE by 2 while wielded. A Nomad may choose to receive this weapon when they first install a Vehicle Heavy Weapon Mount.

Built for MAX-TAC, this helmet contains the most robust optical suite ever packed into headgear. A fully kitted-out model can locate and track threats in any environment, while its nano-alloy easily resists small arms fire without over-encumbering its user. To put it simply, the Max-Helm’s capabilities are as insane as its users are.

SP 16 Head Armor with an Armor Penalty of -1 to REF, and -2 to DEX and MOVE. All ablation this armor would suffer is reduced by 1 (Minimum 0). This armor’s SP is not halved by Martial Arts Attacks and Special Moves. Has built-in Smart Ears (w/ Level Damper and Radio Communicator) and modified Smart Glasses with 8 Option Slots for Cybereye Options. This armor is also capable of installing Subdermal Armor Cyberware Enhancements. This armor repairs itself for 1 point of lost SP at the end of each day in which it does not lose SP.

SP: 16

Foundry notes:

  • Corgo's penalty is -1 REF, -2 DEX, -2 MOVE. The sheet applies one penalty to all three stats, so it uses -2; add the difference back by hand for the lighter stat(s).

Its glowing lines may resemble a fashion statement, but in reality, they’re part of a powered exoshell that can accept external cybernetics such as EMP buffers, dermal reinforcements, or even optical camouflage.

“Some use newtech armor kits to move faster or shoot rifles easier. I use ‘em to bolt on so many layers I can headbutt a fuckin’ rocket and not get scratched.” — Anonymous BARGHEST member

Armor Attachment. May only be installed into a piece of Body/Head Armor with an innate Armor Penalty. Installing this requires a DV17 Basic Tech Skill Check, and cannot be removed once installed. The armor’s SP is increased by 3, but its Armor Penalty (if any) is increased by 1 (e.g., Heavy Armorjack [SP13, -2 to REF/DEX/MOVE] becomes SP16 with -3 to REF/DEX/MOVE). On a second installation, the armor’s SP is again increased by 3 (+6 SP Total), and its Armor Penalty to REF is again increased by 1, but its Armor Penalty to DEX and MOVE is instead increased by 2 (e.g., Heavy Armorjack [SP13, -2 to REF/DEX/MOVE] with 2 Superheavy Plates becomes SP19 with -4 to REF and -5 to DEX/MOVE). Further installations do nothing.

Type: Armor Attachment (Body/Head Armor with an Armor Penalty)
Attachment slots: 0

Foundry notes:

  • Armor Enhancement rules: one Enhancement per piece of armor (armor worn on both body and head counts as one piece); not for cyberware armor (Skinweave, Subdermal Armor) or armor that's part of an ACPA or vehicle; SP limits use the armor's fully repaired SP; a Tech installs or removes one in 1 hour with no check; they don't count as Tech Upgrades for Upgrade Expertise. Armor Attachments have no limit per armor unless stated.
  • +3 SP (automated) and +1 to the Armor Penalty.
  • Raise the armor's penalty by hand.

Before Myers declared war, Militech engineers were asked: How can you equip grunts with superheavy armor and weapons without a full ACPA while avoiding cyberpsychosis? Ultimately, they stripped a Linear Frame to its core components and dedicated all hydraulic power to the legs and hips. These ‘Wolfpack’ frames were highly praised during the war, especially by Militech special forces. Nowadays though, the Wolfpack lets BARGHEST lug around giant guns to mow down gangers with.

The Wolfpack Linear Frame can only be bought as an External Frame. For installation as an External Frame, two installations of Interface Plugs are required. While connected properly to the frame, the total REF and MOVE penalty applied to the user (if any) from worn armor and wielded weapons is reduced by 2, or by 1 for any form of MetalGear (Minimum 0). This frame cannot increase the user's BODY in any way, nor modify their HP or Death Save.

Foundry notes:

  • While connected, your total REF and MOVE penalty from worn armor and wielded weapons drops by 2, or by 1 for any Metalgear (minimum 0); apply by hand.
